requirements.title: Records are value or character sequences with three kinds
requirements.definition: A record is a sequence of values or a sequence of characters, need not correspond to a physical entity, and has one of three kinds: formatted, unformatted, or endfile.

pending.record-not-necessarily-physical: No portable oracle exists for absence of a physical entity; fixture plans must avoid assuming physical records or device layout.

requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

S12.2.1-001 I/O records/files runtime fixtures: formatted fixtures recover exact character sequences and the unformatted fixture recovers integer/logical value sequences from records; the endfile fixture observes the named IOSTAT_END condition after explicit and implicit endfile records. These three executable observations cover the three record kinds without observing or assuming any physical record entity.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.

S12.2.1-001 I/O records/files fixture boundaries: These fixtures are single-image positive runtime observations over internal CHARACTER files, scratch external files, and conservative local named files created in the execution working directory and deleted by the program. They assert only exact integers/logicals/characters, LEN before character equality, IOSTAT zero, and equality with the named IOSTAT_END constant. They do not assert byte sizes, record marker layout, IOMSG text, numeric IOSTAT values, ambient file existence, path syntax beyond the chosen local names, preconnected file identity, coarray image interactions, stream/record correspondence, or required diagnostics for mismatched forms/nonexistent files. Remaining facets stay pending with their source-accounting rationale.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11 for source form, names, expressions, execution constructs, and existing declaration/execution foundations. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: later clause 12 connection, specifier, file-position, data-transfer, internal-file, and input/output-item rules; clause 13 formatting; clause 15 defined I/O; clause 16 inquiry intrinsics where future fixtures need them; clauses 3, 5, 14, 17, 18, and 19 where terminology, constants, images, IEEE support, deleted features, or scope/lifetime controls are reached.

accounting.rationale: Defines records and their three kinds.
NOTE explains terminology; it is not normative and creates no requirement.

review_rationale: Batch272 bound reference-validated record, endfile and file-existence fixtures after four review rounds; program restrictions on record kinds remain pending.
